inspiration.observed_pattern: A public analytical SQL example projects population and sample variance alongside population and sample standard deviation for one numeric measure.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored batch-quality report. Fixed measurements are grouped by batch and project AVG, VAR_POP, VAR_SAMP, STDDEV_POP, and STDDEV_SAMP together; a NULL reading verifies aggregate omission, while a singleton batch distinguishes zero population spread from NULL sample spread. The source dataframe, identifiers, and Spark teaching context are not copied.

fixture_notes: Batch 501 has measurements 10.00, 14.00, and NULL, so AVG is 12.00, VAR_POP is 4.00, VAR_SAMP is 8.00, STDDEV_POP is 2.00, and STDDEV_SAMP is approximately 2.8284. Batch 502 has one non-NULL measurement, so population variance and standard deviation are zero while sample variance and standard deviation are NULL.
determinism_notes: Batch IDs and measurement IDs are fixed; the grouped report is ordered by the unique batch ID, and all aggregate inputs are stable. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE quality_measurements (measurement_id INT PRIMARY KEY, batch_id INT NOT NULL, measured_value DECIMAL(10,2) NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT batch_id, AVG(measured_value) AS mean_value, VAR_POP(measured_value) AS population_variance, VAR_SAMP(measured_value) AS sample_variance, STDDEV_POP(measured_value) AS population_spread, STDDEV_SAMP(measured_value) AS sample_spread FROM quality_measurements GROUP BY batch_id ORDER BY batch_id
